title: Enhanced irradiation-resistance in NbMoTaW refractory high-entropy alloy via rhenium addition

questions.broad: For refractory high-entropy alloys intended for high-temperature and irradiation-exposed applications, what intervention could improve mechanical performance while maintaining thermal and irradiation stability? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted improvement relative to an appropriate baseline, the conditions under which it should hold, supporting prior evidence, and an experiment that could falsify it.
questions.problem_constrained: Equal-atomic NbMoTaW is a single-phase BCC refractory high-entropy alloy with excellent mechanical properties at 1600 °C but very poor room-temperature ductility, while its irradiation resistance has primarily been proposed by first-principles calculations. What intervention could improve its room-temperature ductility without compromising its high-temperature mechanical performance or irradiation resistance? State one hypothesis that identifies the intervention and mechanism, predicts outcomes relative to the untreated NbMoTaW baseline under room-temperature, 1600 °C, and irradiation assessments, defines its boundary conditions, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes a falsification experiment.
questions.expert_context: FCC high-entropy alloys lose substantial strength above 800 °C, motivating refractory high-entropy alloys. Equal-atomic, single-phase BCC NbMoTaW retains excellent mechanical properties at 1600 °C but has poor room-temperature ductility, and its irradiation resistance has been inferred computationally rather than established here experimentally. Studies of other refractory high-entropy alloys have found greater irradiation resistance than pure tungsten under helium implantation and self-healing behavior associated with enhanced atomic diffusion and redistribution. However, irradiation-induced amorphization, helium-energy-dependent blistering, and irradiation-enhanced precipitation have also been observed, indicating unresolved phase- and surface-stability risks. Given the need to preserve BCC structural stability and high-temperature mechanical performance while improving room-temperature ductility and irradiation tolerance, what intervention could achieve this balance? Present one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted directional or quantitative outcomes relative to untreated NbMoTaW, the applicable temperature and irradiation boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.
